title: The Artifact documents delegated-signer authority without naming any of its holders
content:
The Ethena instance dedicates a document to "the addresses authorized as `delegatedSigners` in the `ethenaMinter` contract" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.4.1.3.1). Its child, `Addresses Of Delegated Signers` (.3.1.1), contains only: "`delegatedSigner` addresses — These addesses will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact."

Elsewhere in the chunk, deferral affects things that are recoverable by inspection: a RateLimitID can be recomputed from a key, a `Pool` address read from the aToken contract. A signer set cannot be reasoned about from the document at all — its members are chosen by the Relayer at runtime, and the Artifact is the only place a reader could learn who they are.

The combination is the sharp edge: the same instance grants the Relayer unlimited authority to add signers and declines to record the resulting set. Whatever oversight the slot was created to enable is not currently available, and its absence is invisible unless a reader specifically drills to this leaf.

The placeholder is still better than silence — it establishes that this list is *supposed* to be published, which makes it an auditable commitment rather than an undocumented capability. But it means the privilege surface of the Ethena instance is, as documented, unbounded in membership and unlimited in rate.
description: Ethena's Addresses Of Delegated Signers slot states the addresses will be specified in a future iteration, so a high-privilege set is structurally acknowledged but not enumerated for review.
